summary: The IBM Cloud Terraform provider creates and manages IKS and ROKS VPC clusters, worker pools, and add-ons.
sellerNote: Same provider as VPC and PowerVS. Do not treat Schematics as a different product in this view — it is hosted Terraform.

summary: Vault on the cluster is External Secrets Operator, Vault Secrets Operator, and the Vault CSI provider. That is the clean Kubernetes secrets path.
sellerNote: ESO syncs into Kubernetes Secrets. VSO is the Vault-native operator. CSI mounts secrets as volumes. Do not confuse this with IBM Cloud Secrets Manager CSI.

summary: NS1 Connect is an official ExternalDNS provider, so Ingress hostnames publish to NS1 automatically. NS1 also has a Terraform provider for the zones themselves.
sellerNote: Point ExternalDNS at --provider=ns1. Terraform owns the zone; ExternalDNS owns the records.

summary: Verify Access can run on the cluster. Reverse proxy, runtime, and OIDC all ship as containers.
sellerNote: Containers run on IKS. The certified operator in the Red Hat catalog is the ROKS-shaped version of the same idea.

summary: IBM Application Gateway fronts cluster apps and does OIDC back to IBM Verify, so applications do not have to implement the IdP themselves.
sellerNote: Gateway is the front door. Verify is the IdP. This is not App ID Ingress.

summary: Concert can ingest cluster resources for application inventory and can deploy onto the cluster. It is positioned to run Optimize (Turbonomic) and Observe (Instana plus SevOne).
sellerNote: Moving target. Product packaging is ahead of what is consistently deployable. Sell inventory and art of the possible, not a locked topology.

summary: SevOne can scrape container metrics via Prometheus. It remains network and flow monitoring, not cluster operations.
sellerNote: Do not sell SevOne as the Kubernetes ops console. Instana or IBM Cloud Monitoring own cluster ops.

summary: Terraform is the default way to create VPCs, subnets, security groups, VPEs, and landing-zone stacks.
sellerNote: Landing-zone modules are Terraform. Console click-ops is the anti-pattern.

summary: Packer's IBM Cloud builder bakes custom VPC images that Terraform then launches as virtual server instances.
sellerNote: VSI image factory. Not an IKS/ROKS image stream.

summary: Vault can run on VPC VSIs and inject secrets into instance workloads. This is the non-Kubernetes Vault path.
sellerNote: Cluster path is ESO/VSO/CSI. VSI path is Vault on VPC.

summary: Boundary gives identity-based access to VPC workloads without a jump host or client-to-site VPN.
sellerNote: Still mention IBM Cloud client-to-site VPN as the network-tunnel alternative. Boundary is the session broker.

summary: NS1 Connect provides global traffic steering and failover across multi-region VPC front doors.
sellerNote: This is steering, not ExternalDNS. Cluster hostnames are the IKS/ROKS edge.

summary: SevOne can collect cloud flow logs and follow traffic from Direct Link or VPN through Transit Gateway into VPC and back.
sellerNote: The seller picture is DL/VPN → TGW → VPC. Pair with the Infrastructure view for those network chips.

summary: The IBM Cloud Terraform provider manages PowerVS workspaces, networks, and Transit Gateway attachments next to the VPC landing zone.
sellerNote: Same workspace family as VPC. PER plus TGW is still the network path.

summary: NS1 Connect provides the same global traffic steering and failover for PowerVS-fronted applications as for VPC.
sellerNote: Same NS1 conversation as VPC. Power does not run ExternalDNS.

summary: SevOne follows the same cloud flow-log path for PowerVS as for VPC: Direct Link or VPN through Transit Gateway into the attached VPC and back.
sellerNote: PowerVS traffic is visible once it rides TGW into VPC flow logs. There is no separate Power flow-log product.
